svg.title: Example: Design Sprint
svg.desc: Worked example for a fictional team. A3 landscape board for a five-day design sprint: challenge, long-term goal and sprint questions, the team, Monday to Friday panels (map, sketch, decide, prototype, test) with steps and outputs, a results grid for five customer interviews, and the decision on what happens next.
svg.text: Answer a big question in five days: map the problem, sketch ideas, decide, build a realistic prototype and test it with customers.
Decide What to Build · Design Sprint (Jake Knapp, GV) · Map · Sketch · Decide · Prototype · Test
Ask the experts; note “How might we…?”
Pick a target on the map
Sketch solutions alone, in four steps
Straw poll, then the Decider chooses
Build a realistic façade, not the product
Trial run; write the interview script
The team watches and takes notes
“What question, if answered on Friday, would make this week worth it?”
“What did customers do, not just say?”
Decide What to Build · Design Sprint · Learn in Five Days

g.text: would families set up a staples subscription, and keep it?
1 in 4 weekly shoppers has a staples subscription
will they trust auto-add? Can they
change it easily? Will it feel like a lock-in?
first set-up and the first skip
Families set it up without help
They'd pay for it each week
make skip one tap, test again on 20 June: Mei
